title: User Accounts and Permissions
prompt:
Implement registration, login, logout, password reset, and owner-only access to a private page. Test unauthorized requests.

Submission: a small reviewable artifact, relevant tests, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/environment notes. Use synthetic data. Django/Python server code is not executed by CodeLeaf browser preview; local or human review is required.
target_skills: Use Django authentication features instead of storing raw passwords.
Protect a private view and scope private objects to the current user.
expected_output: Use Django’s built-in authentication views and tested forms rather than implementing password hashing yourself.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous access is redirected or denied according to policy.
A different user cannot access another user’s record.
Password reset does not disclose whether a private account exists.
State whether verification was local, static, or human-reviewed.
Do not claim a build/deployment or external integration was tested unless it was actually run.
hints: Start with the built-in User model and auth views.
Use login_required for authentication and an owner filter for object scope.
Do not confuse login with authorization.
grading_method: Required-string smoke check plus human review of technical correctness, tests, safe handling, expected result and reproducibility. This does not execute arbitrary Python/Django code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend owns its uniform XP/idempotency rules.
status_note: Practical exercise from Section C of the supplied Django curriculum; content and grading need review before publication.
